description: The plot illustrates the relationship between the Recent Sequence Ratio and two variables: Perplexity and GPU Memory Ratio. The x-axis represents the Recent Sequence Ratio, ranging from 0 to 100%, with a linear scale and tick labels at intervals of 20%. The left y-axis represents Perplexity, with a linear scale, ranging from 4.2 to 4.7, and tick labels at intervals of 0.1. The right y-axis represents the GPU Memory Ratio, also with a linear scale, ranging from 40 to 100%, and tick labels at intervals of 10%. The plot displays three lines: Perplexity (orange, solid line with circle markers), GPU Memory Ratio (blue, solid line with circle markers), and Full Cache GPU Memory (red, dashed line). The Perplexity line starts at approximately 4.6 at a Recent Sequence Ratio of 0%, decreases to around 4.3 at 40%, remains relatively stable until 80%, and then slightly increases to about 4.35 at 100%. The GPU Memory Ratio line begins at around 40% at a Recent Sequence Ratio of 0%, gradually increases to approximately 50% at 80%, and then sharply rises to nearly 100% at 100%. The Full Cache GPU Memory line remains constant at around 60% across the entire range of Recent Sequence Ratio.
